why:
ADOPTED, issue 1975 (was a Jazzy-only `gap`, "ADOPT: `create_timer` binds a `Clock`; this returns it"). `rclcpp::Timer::get_clock()` and `rclcpp::TimerHandle`'s `timer_->get_clock()` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/timer.hpp`) both answer from the EXECUTOR — `nros_cpp_timer_get_clock_type` -> `Executor::timer_clock_source`, the `TimerHeader::clock_source` field `arena::timer_try_process` itself reads — so the answer cannot drift from what advances the timer. A wall timer answers `RCL_STEADY_TIME` (rclcpp's wall timers are steady too); a `create_timer(clock, …)` timer the clock it was created with.

ONLY THE RETURN TYPE DIFFERS. Upstream returns `const Clock::SharedPtr&`, a reference to a clock the timer co-owns. There is no allocator to own one (RFC-0022), and the handle `Timer::SharedPtr` names is two words with nowhere to keep a reference into, so the accessor returns `rclcpp::detail::ClockValuePtr`: the `Clock` held BY VALUE behind `->` and `*`. `Clock` owns nothing (`rcl_clock_t` has no allocation; the ROS-time override is process-global), so a copy reads the same time. `timer->get_clock()->now()` — what a ported file writes — keeps its spelling. What does not carry over is keeping the result as a `Clock::SharedPtr` (no such alias here): `auto c = t->get_clock();` is a copy of the clock, not a share of it. `explicit operator bool` is false for an uninitialised, released or stale timer — the null a `SharedPtr` test would have caught — where upstream's is never null.

HELD BY: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/jazzy_small_accessors_runtime.cpp` (COMPILE+LINK+RUN on `just check cpp`): steady / ROS / system clocks read back on both the `Timer` and the handle path, false on an empty, released and stale handle; plus `timer_clock_source_reports_the_registered_clock` in `nros-node`.

NO EDITION SCOPE, deliberately: Humble's `TimerBase` has no `get_clock()`, so under Humble this is an ours-only item, and the same row answers it — the accessor and its envelope are the same whichever upstream it is read against.
